title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
statement: Evaluate an arithmetic expression written in **Reverse Polish Notation**, where each operator comes *after* its two operands (`3 4 +` means 3 + 4). The operators are `+ - * /`, and division truncates toward zero.
idea: In this notation an operator always applies to the **two most recent values** — either numbers just read, or results just computed.
*Most recent first* is exactly what a stack gives. Number → push it. Operator → pop two values, combine them, and push the result back.
The first value popped is the **right-hand** operand. That matters for `−` and `/`. At the end, the one value left on the stack is the answer.

complexity.timeWhy: Each token is handled once with O(1) stack work.
complexity.spaceWhy: The stack can hold up to about half of the tokens.

steps.text: Our example: **`tokens = ["4","13","5","/","+"]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
Numbers wait on a stack until an operator comes along to use them.
`4` is a number. Push it onto the stack.
`13` is a number. Push it onto the stack.
`5` is a number. Push it onto the stack.
`/` is an **operator**. It uses the two most recent values, so pop them: first the right-hand one, `num2` = 5, then the left-hand one, `num1` = 13.
13 / 5 = 2.60, truncated toward zero → **2**. Push the result back — it may be an operand for a later operator.
`+` is an **operator**. It uses the two most recent values, so pop them: first the right-hand one, `num2` = 2, then the left-hand one, `num1` = 4.
4 + 2 = **6**. Push the result back — it may be an operand for a later operator.
Every token has been used. The single value left on the stack is the answer: **6**.
